professionalInsights: The NHS Pharmacy Contraception Service provides convenient repeat oral contraception supply where clinically appropriate after assessment.
Blood pressure and medical history review help ensure safe supply — some patients need GP referral instead.
NHS pharmacy clinical services can reduce unnecessary GP appointments for suitable presentations when commissioned locally.
Pharmacist assessment ensures patients receive appropriate care or clear referral — not treatment outside clinical scope.
Pharmacy Contraception Service is most effective when patients understand what to expect before their appointment.
Pharmacist-led assessment ensures care is proportionate, safe and clearly explained.

mythVsFact.myth: Pharmacies can supply any contraceptive method.
mythVsFact.fact: The NHS Pharmacy Contraception Service covers selected oral contraception — other methods may need GP or sexual health clinic access.

mythVsFact.myth: Pharmacy NHS services replace your GP entirely.
mythVsFact.fact: Pharmacy clinical services complement GP care for selected conditions — GPs remain responsible for ongoing and complex medical management.

mythVsFact.myth: Every NHS pharmacy service is free for everyone.
mythVsFact.fact: Eligibility and commissioning vary by service, location and clinical presentation — suitability is confirmed at assessment.
